5. All stream crossings and paved drainage ditch systems will be protected from siltation caused by erosion during and after highway construction.
6. Temporary erosion control measures will also include construction activities outside of the right of way such as waste disposal sites, equipment storage sites and borrow pits.
7. The engineer will have full authority to suspend or limit grading and other operations pending adequate performance of such permanent erosion control measures as finish grading, topsoiling, mulching, matting and seeding and any temporary erosion control measures ordered by the engineer.
8. Water from aggregate washing or other operations containing sediment will be treated by filtration, a settling basin or other means sufficient to reduce the sediment content to not more than that of the stream into which it is discharged.
Special precautions will be taken to insure surface and ground water quality in the area. As buildings and residences are acquired, the associated wells must be sealed off according to requirements established by the Wisconsin Division of Health. Septic tanks must also be cleaned and removed in accordance with Division of Health Standards.
Air quality will be maintained through the following control measures which will be strictly implemented to reduce fugitive dust associated with the construction projects:
1. The contractor, at the discretion of the project engineer, shall be required to use water or a calcium chloride solution to control dust on the grade and haul roads during construction operations.
